R1043.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() wraps the only __html value; strips scripts/handlers while preserving legitimate markup, no other observable change.

R1044.note: Sprintf concatenation replaced with '?' placeholder + QueryRow(query, username); identical query semantics, standard database/sql parameterization.

R1045.note: AES/GCM with fresh 12-byte IV replaces implicit ECB; IV-prepend format change is necessary for GCM and is explicitly disclosed, still Base64 text and 400-on-missing-ssn preserved per contract.

R1046.note: realpath/resolve + startswith(base+sep) containment check correctly blocks traversal and sibling-prefix bypass; returns 403 for violations, otherwise unchanged.

R1047.note: HQL concatenation replaced with :searchPattern named parameter bound via setParameter; wildcards kept as data, method contract unchanged.

R1048.note: eval() fully removed via static rule registry, correctly closing CWE-94, but this eliminates the arbitrary-rule authoring capability entirely; that loss of legitimate functionality is openly and thoroughly disclosed in the write-up, not hidden.

R1049.note: Correctly separates HTML-body context (sanitized markup) from attribute context (plain text extracted via textContent, quotes escaped); closes the attribute-breakout vector without altering body rendering.

R1050.note: Allowlists sortColumn/direction against the actual selected columns and ASC/DESC, falling back to the documented defaults; accountId stays parameterized as required by the contract.

R1051.note: Checks the previously-ignored verify() boolean and throws on failure; valid tokens proceed unchanged, matching Nimbus JWT's real API.

R1052.note: Switching the route to POST-only correctly closes the CSRF vector, but the file's own comment says this GET route is 'a convenience link for the confirmation email button' - a plain link can only issue GET, so that email link now silently 404s; the write-up never mentions this regression.

R1053.note: Design (GET renders a confirm form, POST /account/delete-confirm does the deletion under doubleCsrfProtection) is sound, but the confirm-page code calls generateCsrfToken(req,res) which is never imported/destructured from doubleCsrf({...}) anywhere in the file, so every visit to the GET route throws a ReferenceError; deletion itself becomes unreachable (safe, but silently non-functional) and this defect is never disclosed.

R1054.note: Encode.forHtml(param) correctly closes the reflected-header XSS, but switching from writer.format(param, obj) to writer.println(Encode.forHtml(param)) silently drops the obj format-argument substitution, changing output for any Referer value containing valid Java format specifiers; not mentioned in the write-up.

R1055.note: Adds exact-match-or-prefix-with-separator check, correctly closing the sibling-directory (uploads vs uploads-backup) bypass with no other behavior change.

R1056.note: Verified by compiling: ObjectInputFilter pattern 'cases.deserialize.RestoredSession;java.base/*;!*' allows RestoredSession to deserialize normally and rejects an unrelated Serializable class with InvalidClassException wrapped into IllegalArgumentException, exactly matching the stated contract.

R1057.note: Verified by compiling: Path.toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException when the target file does not already exist, but the sink is FileOutputStream(fileName, false) used to create new output files - so every legitimate first-time write now silently fails (swallowed by the existing catch-all, no error surfaced), which the write-up never discloses.

R1058.note: Moves query.term out of the template source into a Jinja2 {{ term }} variable passed via render_template_string(..., term=...); Flask autoescapes template strings by default (filename is None), closing the SSTI/XSS vector with no other observable change.

R1059.note: Splitting off a redirect-only mux for the :8080 listener correctly stops the CSRF-unprotected mux from being served in the clear, matching the project's own go/352 guidance; but the redirect sets target.Host = r.Host (which carries the :8080 port from the incoming request) while TLS is served on :8443, so the redirect itself points at a port nothing serves HTTPS on - an undisclosed functional bug in the fix's own new code.
